limitations: Four timed samples per durable-write path, eight per CPU/read path; descriptive local timings, not a production latency benchmark.
No Electron IPC serialization, real renderer parse/Markdown/layout, Windows/VARM/remote disk, LLM latency or tokenizer inference measured.
Source-level scaling and payload-volume estimates are distinguished from observed timings.
Synthetic data max 5,000,000 JSON bytes, all owned files removed after run.

methodology.compiledActualSource: esbuild bundle of app/electron/service.ts loaded in a temporary Node process; actual AtomicStore and WorkbenchService methods, including validateState and durable fsync/rename
methodology.syntheticShape: 4 projects, 8 or 40 tasks/sessions, 20 messages/session, built-in profiles loaded from current workbench. ASCII content padded to exactly 500000 / 5000000 JSON bytes.
methodology.timedWriteMutation: Append five ASCII characters to one message; store.update also increments revision, service.change performs its actual revision increment and notification revision read.
methodology.warmup: One unreported call immediately before each sampled method.
methodology.samples: 4 durable writes per method/case; 8 read/CPU samples; raw values included.
methodology.revisionBroadcast: emit callback only counts, no attached renderer. threePublicSnapshotReads measures 3 actual host snapshot reads, not IPC/rendering.
methodology.retainedScope: Task description set to 12000 ASCII chars; 10 calls to actual buildPrompt(hasContext=true) with short distinct follow-ups. No model prompts sent.

remainingFindings.finding: Streaming persists the entire application state and previous snapshot for every coalesced batch; even a few characters require full clone, validation, two JSON serializations and two fsync/rename snapshots.

sourceEvidence.observation: Streaming flush timer is 60 ms, not 180 ms.
Flush delegates the batch to full change/store.update.
Full draft stringify, plus previous snapshot stringify at 131.
Two atomic snapshot writes per update.
File fsync per atomic snapshot; directory fsync also runs on POSIX.

remainingFindings.observed: 500kB AtomicStore update median 21.167 ms ; 5 MB median 42.462 ms. Actual service.change 5 MB median 43.516 ms. Local Apple M1 / macOS / Node 26.8.1 ; 4 samples each, no Windows inference.
remainingFindings.scalingInference: At a hypothetical sustained 60 ms flush cadence, two 5 MB logical snapshots correspond to 158.95 MiB/s of serialized snapshot bytes. This is a source-based logical volume estimate, not measured physical disk throughput. Serial queue coalescing may lower cadence and increase lag.
remainingFindings.nextSlice: Versioned append-only journal/WAL for small stream deltas and operation intents with periodic snapshots. Preserve single writer, durable acknowledgements, unknown-outcome recovery, crash replay and migration/rollback; do not merely drop fsync or weaken evidence.

remainingFindings.finding: Every state change broadcasts a revision to all windows; every subscribed renderer fetches a full public AppState, including unrelated sessions/history/profile prompts. Host clones again just to read revision. The chat renders all retained messages rather than a windowed transcript.

sourceEvidence.observation: store.read() clones full state to obtain revision.
snapshot() clones full persisted store before dropping private fields.
Global event fans out to every open window when targetWindowId is absent.
Every state.changed schedules refresh; in-flight coalescing avoids overlapping reads but still retains full-state fetch semantics.
session.messages.map renders the whole active transcript; Markdown at 1084.

remainingFindings.observed: Three actual host snapshot reads median 0.680 ms at 500 kB and 7.557 ms at 5 MB. Public snapshot JSON equivalent is 499515 / 4997725 bytes. Electron IPC serialization, React render, Markdown and layout were not timed.
remainingFindings.nextSlice: Revisioned per-project/session deltas with resync/full snapshot only after gap, subscription scoping, lazy transcript pages and virtualized/message-memoized rendering. Keep stale-event generation checks, unread/background execution, multi-window ownership and lossless recoverability.
remainingFindings.finalCandidateMitigation: Only the extra full-store revision clone is removed. Full snapshot fetch/fanout and transcript rendering remain. Baseline sourceEvidence and timings are retained as historical evidence.

remainingFindings.finding: Task goal/scope excerpt up to 12000 characters is added on every turn even after context is established. Input guard checks assembled host string length only, not native CLI history/system/tools/media/output reserve.

sourceEvidence.observation: Common instruction packet is initial-context only.
Goal/scope excerpt is outside initial-context guard and repeats on every turn.
180000 JavaScript-character guard covers host payload only.
Addressed task_history already provides retained context access.

remainingFindings.observed: 10 calls to actual buildPrompt(hasContext=true) each include the 12000-character unchanged scope: 120000 scope characters repeated. This is character measurement, not tokenizer/provider context usage.
remainingFindings.nextSlice: Capture accepted scope revision/fingerprint, send initial scope then bounded meaningful delta/reference when unchanged, with retrieval/resync after CLI compaction/restart. Add provider/runtime-aware context accounting when observable; retain estimated/unknown distinction and reserve output. Never silently delete accepted scope or assume CLI memory from local cache.

finalCandidateNote.verifiedSourceChange: WorkbenchService.change returns result and revision from the same AtomicStore transaction and emits that revision directly. The redundant full-store read/clone for state.changed.revision has been eliminated.
finalCandidateNote.remaining: Full-state clone/serialization/two durable snapshots, full public snapshot fanout and non-windowed transcript rendering, and repeated task-scope/context-budget limitations remain.
finalCandidateNote.timingScope: All timing samples in this report are historical baseline measurements for sourceHashes above, before the redundant revision clone was removed. They are not final-candidate performance measurements.
finalCandidateNote.speedClaim: No final-candidate speedup or benchmark superiority claimed; only the removed operation is confirmed by source inspection.
